audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers claim Fiora can Riposte a Blinding Dart and stun in return: wants.foe[1] "Parry (W) Blinding Shot to cleanse the blind and stun Teemo, turning his primary anti-trade tool into her kill window"; early "she will Riposte (W) immediately to cleanse your Q and stun you in return"; full breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d "Parries + cleanses your blind".
audit.why: Riposte's stab stuns only when Riposte parried an immobilising effect; otherwise it slows. Blind is not an immobilising effect, and Teemo's kit contains no immobilising effect at all — Noxious Trap slows, Blinding Dart blinds, Move Quick is a self-buff. So in a Teemo-vs-Fiora 1v1 Riposte can never produce the stun this entry warns about; the worst case is that she eats the blind and slows you. This is the single most decisive correction in the matchup: the entry currently teaches Teemo to never open with Q, which throws away his best tool for a threat that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Riposting your Blinding Dart costs her the blind and gives her a slow, not a stun — the stun requires her to parry an immobilising effect and you have none. Blind into her Riposte is a bad trade only because you lose the blind, not because you get stunned.
sources: champ-data/_kits/fiora.json (W Riposte: 'This stab slows the first enemy champion hit, or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.')

The two stages that are actually mis-assigned are Level 1 and Levels 4-5, and both are settled by cooldowns rather than opinion: Lunge is 13s at rank 1 against Blinding Dart's flat 7s, and Lunge is 400 range against Teemo's 680 auto/Q range, so at Level 1 she gets one committed approach for every two blinds. audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing explains why the blind is only a partial answer to her Vitals.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags 'Fiora applies on-hit through Lunge (Q)'. Because Lunge deals damage and applies on-hit effects as an ability, it can take a Vital while she is blinded — the blind only stops her basic attacks and the two empowered attacks of Bladework (E). That is why 'blind her and you are safe' is wrong and why Vital positioning still matters through a blind.
audit.corrected: Blind kills her basic attacks and Bladework, but Lunge is an ability and still hits a Vital through the blind — keep rotating your body so the exposed Vital is on the side she cannot lunge to.

edits.before: Fiora owns level 1 cleanly — she can Q-dash onto you before your Blind Shot range forces a decision, and her passive Vital proc at level 1 deals percent-max-HP true damage that your E poison cannot trade back into. Last-hit from maximum auto range, never push toward her, and accept that this is a farm level. The moment she hits level 2 her Lunge (Q) gives her a reliable gap-close that bypasses your E poison kite entirely if she angles it off a minion; do not auto-attack her first because that telegraphs your position and she will Riposte (W) immediately to cleanse your Q and stun you in return. Your only real win here is surviving to level 3 with HP parity — use Move Quick (W) reactively to stay at the edge of your AA range and never let her walk you into her tower where she can take a free Vital.
edits.after: Level 1 is closer than it looks — Lunge is 13 seconds at rank 1 against your flat 7-second Blinding Dart, and her 400 range has to cross your 680, so one blinded approach costs her the whole exchange. Last-hit from maximum auto range and punish every step-in. Once Lunge is ranked it becomes a reliable gap-close that bypasses your E poison kite entirely if she angles it off a minion; do not auto-attack her first because that telegraphs your position and she will Riposte (W) the follow-up. Riposte cannot stun you, though — it only stuns when it parries an immobilising effect and nothing in your kit immobilises — so the worst it does is eat the blind and slow you. Use Move Quick (W) reactively to stay at the edge of your AA range and never let her walk you into her tower where she can take a free Vital.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 belong to Fiora in the straight duel, but your map control starts pulling ahead. Your Q is at or near max rank — use it as bait, not as an opener. Walk up, trigger her Lunge or Riposte reaction, then immediately back off; if she commits Riposte to block nothing she will try to trade into you without it, and that is your window to land Blind Shot and stack three to four E ticks before disengaging with Move Quick. Shroom the tribush, both river entrances, and the lane-center bush behind you — these do not exist to kill her, they exist to punish the Q dash landing spot and slow her enough that Move Quick breaks the gap. Level 6 flips the kill threat: Grand Challenge creates four Vitals that she can chain through your low HP pool in one rotation even through a Blind, so the moment she uses R get off the wave immediately and path toward a mushroom you already placed.

notes: I deliberately did not touch the claim that Fiora's Vitals deal percent-max-HP true damage. It is very likely correct, but the Data Dragon passive text in champ-data/_kits/fiora.json is a truncated tooltip variant ('Fiora has revealed a Vital on this Champion') that carries no damage type, so it is not verifiable from local sources and I was told not to speculate. Same for whether Riposte removes an already-applied blind versus preventing it during the parry window — I only corrected the stun claim, which the kit text settles outright. Residual layer divergence after my edits: content win[] and full phases[] still disagree at Level 3, Level 6, First item and 2+ items. Both charts are now individually consistent with a 52.85% win rate, so I left those alone rather than invent shifts, but somebody should decide which chart is canonical for this champion.
